output.brief: The wrong expiry dates were not caused by operators, the printer firmware, or the agency staff. Printer job records show that from 4 Oct the printer received a shelf-life value of 36 months instead of 24, and printed exactly what it was sent, with no operator overrides. The ERP audit trail shows that on 3 Oct a Regulatory Affairs edit entered 36 months for Veltranol, but with a valid-from date of 1 March 2027. The system appears to have used it early. Earlier lots, and the agency operators' jobs before 4 Oct, were correct. How sure I am: fairly confident about what was not the cause. The link to the ERP edit is likely but not yet proven, because the PackBridge logic has not been checked and the vendor says this should not happen. Next: reset the Veltranol shelf-life values so only the approved 24 months can be read, widen the hold to all Veltranol lots packed since 3 Oct, and add a second-person expiry check at each setup. Check the other products changed in October before deciding on wider action. Do not remove the agency operators or switch off the camera check; neither addresses the cause.
